claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 8259 s3: "A JSON value MUST be an object, array, number, or string, or one of the following three literal names: false null true ... No other literal names are allowed." Grammar: value = false / null / true / object / array / number / string.

RFC 8259 s3 value grammar lists no date kind (false / null / true / object / array / number / string). Second half from prior review: .NET "The JSON format does not directly support dates and times."; STJ "parses and writes DateTime and DateTimeOffset values according to the ISO 8601-1:2019 extended profile" (as strings).

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). "The System.Text.Json default is to throw exceptions for comments because the RFC 8259 specification doesn't include them." / "By default, comments and trailing commas are not allowed in JSON."

RFC 8259 s6: one grammar "number = [ minus ] int [ frac ] [ exp ]", no integer/decimal kind; "This specification allows implementations to set limits on the range and precision of numbers accepted." So the receiver decides; .NET maps "All numeric types, for example Int32, Decimal or Double" to Number (prior review).

RFC 8259 s8.1: "JSON text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8 [RFC3629]." Claim and lesson s4 ("JSON sent between separate systems must use UTF-8") match.
